messages.author: 3afa2b67ef806635
messages.subject: Odd behavior from data_frame
parts:
Hi All,

dplyr's data_frame is a handy alternative to data.frame but I'm getting some odd behavior when attempting to tack a new variable onto an existing tbl_df. I'm not really sure what it's doing. Any ideas?

Thanks,
Bob

> x <- 1:5
> y <- 11:15
> mytbl <- data_frame(x,y)
> mytbl
Source: local data frame [5 x 2]

  x  y
1 1 11
2 2 12
3 3 13
4 4 14
5 5 15
> class(mytbl)
[1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame"
> z <- 101:105
> data.frame(mytbl, z)
  x  y   z
1 1 11 101
2 2 12 102
3 3 13 103
4 4 14 104
5 5 15 105
> data_frame(mytbl, z)   
Source: local data frame [5 x 2]

      mytbl   z
1  <int[5]> 101
2  <int[5]> 102
3 <NULL[0]> 103
4 <NULL[0]> 104
5 <NULL[0]> 105

> sessionInfo()
R version 3.1.1 (2014-07-10)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)

locale:
[1] LC_COLLATE=English_United States.1252

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Odd behavior from data_frame
parts:
You can't use data_frame to add new variables to an existing
data_frame - you will get a data frame where one column contains a
data frame.

Hadley

messages.author: 3afa2b67ef806635
messages.subject: Re: Odd behavior from data_frame
parts:
So that's a feature rather than a bug I guess. That's unfortunate since two of the first things I would want to teach people about dplyr is what data_frame does, and how important it is to save row names as a variable. It would be natural to address both with the example:

 mydata <- data_frame(id = row.names(mydata), mydata)

Bob

You can't use data_frame to add new variables to an existing
